summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a new payment called the Farm Household Allowance for farmers and their partners experiencing financial difficulty.
The allowance would provide time-limited income support and funding for advice and training, and would be aligned with social security payments like newstart and youth allowances.

The Farm Household Allowance would replace the Exceptional Circumstances Relief Payment and be available regardless of the cause of hardship, unlike the current drought policy that relies on a climatic trigger.
changes: Establishes the Farm Household Allowance as a new form of financial assistance.
Replaces the existing Exceptional Circumstances Relief Payment.
Shifts the focus of farmer assistance from crisis response to preparedness and risk management.
summary.affected: Farmers and their partners in financial hardship.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Introduced the Farm Household Support Bill, replacing the 1992 Act with a new farm household allowance from 1 July 2014 providing up to three years of income support, and noted that during the 2008 to 2009 financial year over 30,000 farm families relied on the Exceptional Circumstances Relief Payment introduced in 1999, with a new $3,000 training grant also available.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Introduced the companion Farm Household Support (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill, which repeals the redundant Farm Household Support Act 1992 and makes transitional arrangements so recipients can move smoothly onto the new farm household allowance.

speeches.speaker: Joel Fitzgibbon
speeches.brief: Said the opposition supports the Farm Household Support Bill's new safety net payment for struggling farmers, noting it costs $99.4 million over four years with $37.6 million allocated to administration, and asked the minister to explain that administrative cost.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, describing a $324 million drought assistance package that includes $280 million in concessional loans and a farm household allowance for farmers regardless of on-paper asset value, replacing the previous transitional farm family payment.

speeches.speaker: Clare O'Neil
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, noting the farm household allowance provides up to three years of income support from 1 July 2014, replacing the exceptional circumstances relief payment, but criticised the government for abolishing the Standing Committee on Primary Industries and delaying the bill despite months-old drought conditions.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, citing national agricultural exports worth $38 billion last year, and outlining the government's $320 million drought package, including $280 million in concessional loans, water infrastructure funding, and mental health services for farming communities.

speeches.speaker: Mark Coulton
speeches.brief: Said his electorate has been the epicentre of the drought, with the Walgett Shire, which normally produces a million tonnes of wheat, producing none last year, and welcomed the Farm Household Support Bill's $280 million in concessional loans.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Praised Camp Cobbold, a social development program supporting geographically isolated families in north-west Queensland, and noted the $10.7 million for mental health services included in the Farm Household Support Bill being debated.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, said 80 per cent of Queensland's landmass, about 1.5 million square kilometres, is in drought, and criticised the mandatory Horticulture Code of Conduct as unnecessary red tape for Brisbane Markets, a $1 billion-turnover business employing up to 4,000 people, given only 28 inquiries and six mediations occurred under the code in three years.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: Detailed the government's drought package, including an interim Farm Household Allowance effective from 3 March, $280 million in concessional loans of up to $1 million or 50 per cent of eligible debt at four per cent for five years, and $10 million for social and mental health support in farming communities.

speeches.speaker: Bob Katter
speeches.brief: Disputed the member for Wannon's optimistic outlook for Australian agriculture, arguing no one in the sector would share that confidence, and previewed a rebuttal using ABS statistics.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Hogan
speeches.brief: Acknowledged the agricultural sector's serious challenges raised by the member for Kennedy, and said one of his electorate's biggest private employers, an abattoir, was harmed by the live export ban, which caused cattle prices to fall significantly.

speeches.speaker: George Christensen
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, said the carbon tax equates to about $20,000 per farmer in the sugar industry, and described his coastal North Queensland electorate of Dawson, stretching about 400 kilometres, where Bowen alone produces two-thirds of Australia's winter tomato crop.

speeches.speaker: Tony Pasin
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill for his 64,000 square kilometre electorate of Barker, cited national agricultural production worth over $47 billion and exports worth about $38 billion last year, and detailed the bill's $2.55 million net farm assets test excluding the family home.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, said a John Deere harvester costing $400,000 in the United States costs $800,000 in Australia, and noted Queensland's dairy farmer numbers fell from 2,500 to fewer than 500 in a decade, while the Lockyer Valley alone produces about $250 million in produce annually.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Highlighted agriculture's economic contribution, noting Australia turned a forecast $100 million loss in January into a $1.4 billion trade surplus, driven substantially by exports including more than six million tonnes of wheat from Western Australia and renewed live cattle and sheep trade.

speeches.speaker: Joel Fitzgibbon
speeches.brief: Announced Labor's bipartisan support for the Farm Household Support (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill, criticised the government's agricultural white paper for omitting climate change and natural resource sustainability from its terms of reference, and cited a report suggesting $500 billion to $600 billion in investment is needed to capitalise on Asian food production opportunities.
